design: A rounded low-poly pocket console with satin dyed-ABS, soft contact collars, original gecko keys and grouped pixel pigment
scope: Restore the approved rounded dyed-plastic cover identity: broad quiet pigment planes, restrained species marks, lower chroma, satin plastic reflections and localized handling wear. Keep the eight real species moldings and original three navigation gecko glyphs. Give each miniature a separately posed rest and a matching loose cord.

authoring.paint: Shell pigment restores continuous side shade fields, quiet crown/chin surfaces and sparse species-specific accents instead of large graphic wraps. Approved base hues are muted by about22 percent chroma; ink/key/center/light values remain fixed. Each miniature retains its independent anatomical pattern and mildly muted matching colors. Shell192x256/248x164 and charm64x112 packed Closest atlases keep native pixel density.
authoring.lighting: The painted casing uses96 percent physical dielectric response with4 percent illustration fill: roughness about.37,coat.065/roughness.34,specular.47. Quiet fine molded grain and slow reflection variation only affect sheen; three handling areas gain gentle polishing. Five short surface-projected scuffs plus a few authored corner rubs supply localized wear. Lighting is the approved broad soft setup. Other surfaces and key glyphs retain prior materials.
authoring.output: 2x antialiased silhouette: portrait1120x1640 (left/top/right/bottom40/140/40/40 logical), landscape1720x1060 (120/80/120/40). Browser frame bounds and optical aperture stay at their original body-relative coordinates.
authoring.geometry: The broad convex front has smooth normal transitions, with sharp seams, recess walls and the low-poly silhouette retained. The screen hood has a uniform optical rim. Small ports, switch and speaker slots are actual shallow cavities with backing and molded lips, projected point-by-point to the skin. Browser screen aperture, key XY bounds and glyph placement remain fixed.
authoring.charm: All eight real species anatomy meshes and their five-digit feet remain unchanged. Individual tabletop rests use different angles: leopard−21°,tokay38°,day−67°,crested76°,fat-tail−3°,mossy132°,electric−128°,stone57°. Each has separately fitted placement and cord handles in portrait and landscape; the threaded cord stays visible above the convex cover before dropping to the tabletop.

paint_color_origins: Species morphology, natural color-pattern evidence and palette-stage limits are maintained together in species[]. All runtime pigment is newly authored for the plastic miniature and shell.
limits: References inform drawing methods only. No third-party meshes or textures are used. The only functional browser controls on the housing are the three navigation keys; other small hardware marks are illustrative.
button_art: The sole bitmap source is brand.mjs avatarVariants[0..2]. Every original pixel retains exact XY, size and gaze; its internal surface patches follow only Z so ink remains visible on the convex key caps.
refinement_review: Compare the restored satin cover with the approved pre-species shell: the uninterrupted convex plastic surface carries the volume again, while biological patterns remain subordinate. Verify eight truly distinct rests/cords, frozen button bitmap/XY/ink colors, unchanged casing geometry, screen clearance and viewport fit.
charm_review: Reference photos and field papers checked for all eight species. Corrected day tail length and nose-eye stripe, crested triangular skull and eyelash crest, natural fat-tail length and toe type, and asymmetric Moorish saddles. Original button glyph bitmap and XY are preserved.

morphology: Long relatively large triangular skull and snout; a narrow neck rather than a round humanoid head.
Conspicuous paired eyelash ridges above eyes continue as two sawtooth/triangular-scale crests along upper back.
Expanded pad-bearing fingers; five digits including smaller first digit; fine granular skin, no large stone-gecko warts.
Moderately thick prehensile tail that tapers to a slim adhesive tip, roughly 80–92% snout-vent length; an intact-tail variant is chosen.
pattern: Warm tan/peach/ochre ground, dark irregular lateral tiger bars or diagonals rather than even full black body bands.
Pale cream paired crests/dorsal margins are the strongest transferable shell signature: run two broken pale rails around shoulders and side frame, with darker angled flank strokes.
Crest detail belongs to geometry; do not rely only on painting a line onto the same base mesh.

morphology: Broad flattened squat body and relatively large broad tapering head, shorter neck and short sturdy splayed limbs.
Five distal-expanded leaf/spoon-like toes, distinct from spherical frog-like discs.
Several prominent staggered longitudinal rows of angular/conical dorsal tubercles; carry smaller rough rings onto original tail.
Tapering rough tail, less fleshy than fat-tail; original tail length close to body length by official 12–16cm TL and6–8cm SVL range, so avoid anatomically stumpy tail unless explicitly regenerated.
pattern: Grey-brown ground with four/five irregular broken darker transverse saddles; pale margins and darker wart centers.
Shell should use broken stony saddle edges with staggered small wart-like pigment clusters, not neat straight fat-tail bands.
Keep mottles muted but sufficiently contrasting so the design is distinct from smooth moss patches.
